Hi all — technical clarification below, requested in a concise scope matrix style to match Acme's auditor requirements.

1) Redwood Hosted (public API) — IN SCOPE (our Oct 2026 test)- Components included: Redwood public API gateway, control plane (model registry, routing), multi-tenant inference runtime on Redwood-managed GPUs, authentication/authorization layers we operate, and token handling systems.- Notes: customer data processed via Hosted API is within the tested runtime; we exercised auth flows, token handling, and model execution paths.

2) Redwood Dedicated (Redwood-managed capacity, separate tenant but hosted in our cloud) — IN SCOPE (tested)- Components included: dedicated GPU pools managed by Redwood, tenant isolation controls at the runtime level, autoscaling hooks, and the control plane interactions.- Notes: For Dedicated that is still managed by Redwood in our environment, the runtime and control plane components are the same codebase exercised in Hosted tests.

3) Dedicated deployed into Customer VPC (customer-provisioned networking with Redwood-managed runtime overlay) — PARTIAL SCOPE / CONDITIONAL- What we control: runtime container images, orchestration agent, and model-serving binaries.- What customer controls: VPC networking, host OS, and cloud provider account resources.- Testing boundary: Redwood can include runtime and agent components but not host OS or VPC-level controls unless Acme authorizes agent-level testing and provides temporary access (or we coordinate with your chosen vendor to test host-level config).

4) Private/VPC (Redwood control plane deployed into customer VPC + optional on-prem agents) — OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood-owned pen tests unless specifically contracted- Rationale: When control plane components run in Acme's VPC under your cloud account, they fall under your scope. We will support, provide artifacts (binaries, configs), and can run a coordinated test with Pennest if Acme requests and signs the access addendum.

5) Fully On‑prem / Air‑gapped installations — OUT OF SCOPE for Redwood tests- These environments are owned and operated by the customer; Redwood does not run tests there. We provide guidance docs and assist with a scoping checklist for third-party testers.

Remediation status (for medium findings from Oct 2026 summary):- MED-01 (token replay risk): mitigated (patch deployed 2026-10-12) — mitigation verified by internal regression tests; external verification available on request.- MED-02 (misconfigured CORS header on admin endpoints): mitigated (2026-10-15) — scope confirmed to admin tiers only; not customer-facing.- MED-03 (insecure default SSH key rotation policy in a build node): mitigated (rotations automated 2026-10-22) and we rotated keys; we have rotation logs and a Jira ticket: JIRA-SEC-4521.

If Acme wants Pennest to validate those mitigations, we can provide a short checklist and a test window; Pennest should be able to re-test the mitigations against the Redwood-managed endpoints. For anything inside Acme's VPC or on-prem instances, Pennest will need the access you control.

Technical artifacts we can provide to Pennest on NDA: runtime binary checksums, container image manifests, IP ranges for test windows (we'll provide ephemeral ranges per engagement), and redacted issue tracker exports.
